Privacy

Local text should remain local.

CommonCopy is designed to complete its core job without an account, a remote server, or hidden collection of the text you type.

Phrase storage

Your categories, phrases, settings, favorites, and recent-use information are stored in a readable JSON file under your Windows user profile. CommonCopy does not upload this file.

Clipboard use

When you choose a phrase, CommonCopy temporarily places its text on the Windows clipboard and sends the normal paste shortcut to the application you were using. When you explicitly choose Save highlighted text…, it sends the normal copy shortcut once and reads that selected text into the save form. CommonCopy does not continuously inspect the clipboard or application content. It attempts to restore the clipboard’s previous text afterward, and clipboard contents are never transmitted.

Global input access

Windows input hooks are used only to detect the configured Ctrl + Right Click gesture and global keyboard shortcut. CommonCopy does not record typed text, build a keystroke history, or continuously capture application content.

Website data

This initial website includes no cookies, advertising network scripts, tracking pixels, or analytics. If aggregate website analytics are introduced later, this page will be updated before they are enabled.

Sensitive information

CommonCopy is not an encrypted secrets vault. Do not store passwords, access tokens, private keys, recovery codes, or other authentication credentials in it.

Questions and changes

The public repository will provide an issue tracker and security-reporting instructions when the project launches. Material privacy changes will be documented in the project changelog and on this page.
